title: Exceptional-curve injection for a normalized dominating graph
statement:
Let $X,Y,X'$ be normal integral excellent Noetherian schemes of topological dimension $2$, excellence meaning excellence on every affine coordinate ring [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $f:Y	o X$ and $g:X'	o X$ be proper morphisms inducing isomorphisms of function fields, and identify all three fields with $K$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sc-function-field]. In $P=Y	imes_X X'$ take the reduced closed subscheme $W$ whose underlying space is the closure of the point $\operatorname{Spec}K=P	imes_X\operatorname{Spec}K$, and let $
u:Y'=W^
u	o W$ be its normalization in $K$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sc-normalization]. Thus $W$ is the component dominating $X$, rather than the whole fibre product. Then $
u$ is finite, $Y'$ is normal integral excellent Noetherian of dimension $2$, and the projections $p:Y'	o Y$ and $f':Y'	o X'$ are proper and induce isomorphisms of function fields [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. For any such morphism $a:V	o T$ write $B(a)$ for the integral closed one-dimensional subschemes of $V$ mapped to one point, using reduced induced scheme structures. For every $C'\in B(f')$, the reduced image $C=p(C')$ belongs to $B(f)$, and $C'\mapsto C$ is injective. The map $p$ is an isomorphism on an open neighbourhood of the generic point $\eta_C$ of each such $C$, and it identifies $\mathcal O_{Y,\eta_C}=\mathcal O_{Y',\eta_{C'}}$ inside $K$ [def-sc-generic-point]. If $x'=f'(C')$ and $x=f(C)$, then $x'$ and $x$ are closed, $g(x')=x$, and $\kappa(x')/\kappa(x)$ is finite [def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Tag 0BBT (resolve-lemma-dominate-by-normalized-blowing-up), proof third paragraph and its injection BadCurves(f′) to BadCurves(f). The construction is the normalization of the reduced component dominating X, to make the asserted birational projections valid. It works for an arbitrary proper birational g between normal excellent surfaces; no point-blowup or termination assertion is included.

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of [lem-per-normal-modification-codimension-one] to $f$ and $g$. Each target is Noetherian, each source is reduced, and each map is birational because it is dominant between integral schemes and identifies their generic local fields. Intersect the resulting isomorphism opens to get an open $U\subset X$ containing the generic point, with $Y_U=X'_U=U$. By the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product], $P_U=U$. The closure of its generic point is irreducible; its reduced induced scheme $W$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], and $W_U=U$. Thus the projections $W\to Y$, $W\to X'$ and $W\to X$ identify generic local fields with $K$ [def-sc-function-field].

source.place: Tag 0BBT, normalized dominating component in the third proof paragraph; Tag 0BFP (1)

proof.text: Both projections of $P$ are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Their restrictions to the closed subscheme $W$ are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], and $W\to X$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. Apply [lem-per-normal-surface-exceptional-curves] to this last morphism: its target is the given normal integral excellent Noetherian surface, its source $W$ is integral, and its function-field map is an isomorphism by Step 1. It gives finiteness and properness of $\nu$, and normality, integrality, excellence, Noetherianness and dimension $2$ of $Y'$. Composing $\nu$ with $W\to Y$ and $W\to X'$ gives proper $p,f'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. Normalization in $K$ preserves that generic field, as also asserted by [lem-per-normal-surface-exceptional-curves]; hence both projections are birational, with the specified identifications in $K$.

source.place: Tag 0BBT, first and third proof paragraphs (normalization and proper projections)

proof.text: Fix $C'\in B(f')$ and put $x'=f'(C')$. Apply [lem-per-normal-surface-exceptional-curves] to $f':Y'\to X'$; its normalization is an isomorphism since $Y'$ is normal. Therefore $x'$ is closed and $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(x')}\kappa(\eta_{C'})=1$. Put $x=g(x')$. Properness makes $g$ closed [pqf-lem-proper-basic], so $x$ is closed. The fibre $X'_x$ is of finite type over $\kappa(x)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] and [pqf-lem-proper-basic]. The point $x'$ is closed in this fibre, so [lem-kun-closed-point-field] gives $[\kappa(x'):\kappa(x)]<\infty$. The commuting projections give $fp(C')=\{x\}$.

source.place: Tag 0BBT, third proof paragraph; Morphisms Tag 01TB (lemma-closed-point-fibre-locally-finite-type) for residue fields

proof.text: Suppose $p(C')=\{y\}$. Since $p$ is closed [pqf-lem-proper-basic], $y$ is closed in $Y$. Applying [lem-kun-closed-point-field] to the proper fibre $Y_x$ (proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], finite type by [pqf-lem-proper-basic]) gives $[\kappa(y):\kappa(x)]<\infty$. Write $z=\eta_{C'}$ and $w=\nu(z)\in W\subset P$. The residue-field point of $w$ lies over $(y,x')$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the scheme of pairs of residue-field points is $Q=\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(y)\otimes_{\kappa(x)}\kappa(x'))$. Its points correspond precisely to points of $P$ over $(y,x')$, with the same residue fields (and the closed immersion $W\subset P$ does not change the residue field [def-weil-closed-immersion]): on affine charts this is localization at the two primes and quotient by them. This last description follows directly from the displayed tensor-product model. The algebra defining $Q$ is finite-dimensional over $\kappa(x)$, generated as a vector space by tensors of members of finite bases. Its quotient by any prime is a finite-dimensional domain, hence a field by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field]. Consequently $\kappa(w)$ is finite over $\kappa(x)$.

source.place: Tag 0BBT, third proof paragraph: why a contracted curve cannot map to a point under both projections

proof.text: For completeness compute the residue extension for the finite map $\nu$ at $z$ rather than assuming that an arbitrary morphism has finite residue fields. Take an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset W$ of $w$. Its inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ finite over $A$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. If $\mathfrak q\subset B$ represents $z$ and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap A$, the algebra $D=B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is spanned over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ by the images of finite $A$-module generators of $B$. Its quotient by the prime representing $z$ is a finite-dimensional domain, hence a field by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field]. This quotient is therefore already its own fraction field $\kappa(z)$, proving $[\kappa(z):\kappa(w)]<\infty$. Under the supposition in Step 4 it follows that $\kappa(z)$ is finite over $\kappa(x)$, hence over its intermediate subfield $\kappa(x')$. Its transcendence degree over $\kappa(x')$ is then zero, contradicting the value $1$ from Step 3. Thus $p(C')$ is not a point. This computation is just finite generation, base extension and the cited field criterion; it does not require a further geometric comparison lemma.

source.place: Tag 0BBT, third proof paragraph: finiteness of normalization excludes simultaneous contraction

proof.text: Let $C=p(C')$ with its reduced induced structure. Properness of $p$ makes this an irreducible closed subset of $Y$ [pqf-lem-proper-basic]. It is proper since $f(C)=\{x\}$ whereas $f$ is dominant onto a two-dimensional scheme. From [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], every chain of irreducible closed subsets in $C$ can be prolonged by $Y$, so $\dim C\leq1$. Step 5 excludes a singleton. An irreducible zero-dimensional closed subset of a scheme is a singleton: if it contained a different point from its generic point, that point's closure would be a nonempty proper irreducible closed subset. Existence and uniqueness of that generic point is [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Thus $\dim C=1$. Its reduced irreducible structure is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], so $C\in B(f)$. The identities $x=f(C)$ and $g(x')=x$, and the closedness and residue-field finiteness demanded in the statement, are exactly those established in Step 3.

source.place: Tag 0BBT, third proof paragraph: the reduced image belongs to BadCurves(f)

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-normal-surface-exceptional-curves] to $f:Y\to X$. Because $Y$ is normal its normalization is an isomorphism, so for the curve $C\in B(f)$ it supplies that $\mathcal O_{Y,\eta_C}$ is a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. The point $\eta_C$ has codimension one in the sense of [lem-per-normal-modification-codimension-one], namely $\dim\mathcal O_{Y,\eta_C}=1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]: in a local principal ideal domain that is not a field, $0$ is prime, every nonzero prime is maximal and hence equals $\mathfrak m\neq0$, so the longest chain of primes is $0\subsetneq\mathfrak m$. Apply clause (2) of [lem-per-normal-modification-codimension-one] to $p:Y'\to Y$: $Y$ is Noetherian, and $p$ is proper birational with reduced source by Step 2. There is an open neighbourhood $V_C$ of $\eta_C$ such that $p^{-1}(V_C)\to V_C$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0BBT, third proof paragraph, codimension-one isomorphism; Tag 0BFP (2)

proof.text: The continuous closed map $p$ sends the closure of $\eta_{C'}$ to the closure of its image, so $p(\eta_{C'})$ is the unique generic point $\eta_C$ [pqf-lem-proper-basic, def-sc-generic-point, lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Step 7 gives exactly one point above $\eta_C$. Consequently any two curves in $B(f')$ with image $C$ have the same generic point, hence the same underlying closure and the same reduced induced closed subscheme. This proves injectivity. The same open isomorphism identifies their generic local rings by the actual structural stalk map. Its map at the generic point of the whole integral surface is the identity of the already identified field $K$ (Step 2); taking germs embeds both local rings into this $K$ [def-sc-function-field]. Thus the identification is the equality $\mathcal O_{Y,\eta_C}=\mathcal O_{Y',\eta_{C'}}\subset K$ required in the statement.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q39-17932794f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item's statement, which is unchanged from base, and all 8 steps against every cited statement, Stacks 0BBT (third proof paragraph) and 0BFP (all four clauses). The mathematics is correct. Steps 1-2: the codim-one node, clause (1), applied to f and g gives an isomorphism open U with P_U = U, so the dominating component W is integral with function field K. lem-per-normal-surface-exceptional-curves applies to W->X, with no dim W = 2 assumed, and gives finite nu, a normal excellent 2-dimensional Y' and proper birational p, f'. Steps 3-5: x' and x are closed and kappa(x') is finite over kappa(x) by lem-kun-closed-point-field (a) on the finite-type fibre. If p(C') were a point, the residue fields of the tensor-product model and of the finite map nu would make kappa(eta_C') finite over kappa(x'), contradicting trdeg 1. Step 6: C is in B(f), using chain dimension and sobriety. Step 8: closed map plus a single point in the fibre gives injectivity and equality of local rings inside K. Edge cases checked: g = id, f = id, blowing up a point that f does not contract. The parent's uses all match the statement. No new nodes; the 0BBT/BadCurves grep finds no duplicate. FIX (C4/C1): Step 7 proved topological codimension one, but the codim-one node, clause (2), needs dim O_{Y,eta_C} = 1, and nothing cited links the two. Rewrote Step 7 to read dim = 1 off the DVR clause (local PID, not a field, so its primes are 0 and m), citing def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring and def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring, and recomputed proof_deps.
